task.problem:
Let X be a connected compact complex n-fold, with a smooth strictly positive probability volume dV and dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial. All quasi-psh and psh potentials are genuine canonical upper representatives; arbitrary almost-everywhere modifications are excluded. A smooth real background theta is nef if theta+epsilon h has a strictly positive smooth dd^c-potential representative for every epsilon>0, where h is a fixed Hermitian metric; it is big if theta+dd^c u>=delta h for some delta>0 and genuine global quasi-psh u. Neither property assumes d-closedness. The extended Monge-Ampere measure MA_ext_theta is the genuine non-pluripolar product with smooth-background correction terms. For Hermitian h, v_-(h) is the infimum of integral MA_h(u) over all bounded genuine h-psh potentials. For nonzero f>=0 in L1(dV), let c_h(min(f,k)) be the scalar of the supremum-normalized continuous bounded-density equation and b_h(f)=lim_k c_h(min(f,k)); equivalently b_h(f) is the largest coefficient a>=0 of a genuine subsolution MA_ext_h(s)>=a f dV. If b_h(f)>0, the greatest exponential solution u_lambda of MA_ext_h(u_lambda)=exp(lambda u_lambda)f dV exists for every lambda>0, is genuine, has finite mass, and dominates every exponential subsolution. Set v_lambda=u_lambda-sup_X u_lambda and c_lambda=exp(lambda sup_X u_lambda). Known scalar and measure convergence c_lambda->b_h(f) and exp(lambda u_lambda)f->b_h(f)f in L1 does not by itself prove convergence of v_lambda. The available lower barrier contains the actual scalar error lambda^(-1)log(c_lambda/b_h(f)); this term cannot be discarded. If v_-(h)>0, every L1 cluster of v_lambda converges in capacity and solves the exact threshold equation in the zero-reference envelope class, but this still need not identify a single potential. For a smooth big possibly nonclosed theta define P_theta(a) as the usc envelope of genuine theta-psh potentials <=a, u preceq phi as u<=phi+C, and P_theta[u](phi)=(lim_{C->infinity}P_theta(min(u+C,phi)))^*. An ordinary model reference has sup phi=0 and P_theta[phi](0)=phi. The relative envelope class E_env(X,theta,phi) consists of u preceq phi such that for every real t>=1 there exists a genuine theta-psh a with t^(-1)a+(1-t^(-1))phi<=u; the convex inequality is meaningful even at common poles. Do not replace this definition in unrestricted settings by zero-obstacle envelope equality, whose converses need additional hypotheses. Ordinary bounded type u~phi means mutual inequalities up to finite constants, interpreted with common poles. When using prescribed references, state which of these classes is used and how the exponential density is weighted at poles. Original S05 asks for conditions ensuring whole-family convergence of normalized greatest positive-exponent solutions to a canonically selected zero-exponent potential, first for fixed density and reference and then for varying model references and densities while retaining the limiting type. A useful selection must have a proved variational or order characterization, particularly for L1 data; uniqueness of the scalar alone is insufficient. General zero-exponent potentials are not unique, including smooth or real-analytic density examples, so do not claim universal potential uniqueness. Additional already established background: for nonzero Lp data p>1 and an arbitrary smooth big theta in minimal ordinary type, the entire centered exponential family u_lambda-lambda^(-1)log c(f) converges locally uniformly off an analytic strict barrier and in L1. Its limit is the greatest continuous minimal-type critical subsolution whose integrals against every supporting probability of r->log c(f)-log c(exp(r)f) are <=0. Smooth strictly positive or specified semipositive dual maximizers also give existing selection results. These known cases are not new S05 progress. No new selection criterion, density family, reference family, theorem or proof is supplied.

# Exact statement-only targets: arbitrary Hermitian factor and moving logarithmic references

Every following claim is an unproved target. No author argument, previous verdict, source-reading receipt or candidate proof is supplied. TeX shorthands: Pone is P1, ddc is the original operator, PSH is genuine canonical psh in the stated background, MA is the actual non-pluripolar corrected product, and E_env is exactly the original relative stretching class. Preserve all canonical conventions, common poles and ordinary bounded type.

Let $(Y,\kappa)$ be any connected compact Hermitian $k$-fold, $k\geq1$,
normalized by $\int_Y\kappa^k=1$. On $X=\Pone_x\times Y$ put $N=k+1$,
take the mass-one Fubini--Study form $\omega_1$ and use
$dW=\omega_1\wedge\kappa^k$. Pullbacks are implicit; $\kappa$ need not be closed.
Fix $a,d>0$, a smooth positive nonconstant $b=b(x)$, and continuous $H=H(x)>0$.
Set
\[
 \theta=(a+d)\omega_1+b\kappa,\quad
 \eta=a\omega_1+b\kappa,\quad f=N b^kH,\quad
 m=\int_{\Pone}H\omega_1,\quad c_0=\frac am.
\]
Both backgrounds are claimed to be smooth strictly positive and genuinely nonclosed; prove these assertions independently.
With $D=\{Z_0=0\}\times Y$, write
\[
 \ell=\frac{|Z_0|^2}{|Z_0|^2+|Z_1|^2},\qquad
 \psi=d\log\ell,\qquad
 \theta+\ddc\psi=\eta+d[D].
\]
The canonical value of $\psi$ on $D$ is $-\infty$.

For $K=a+d$, $R=a/d$ and
$C_*=K\log(K/d)-a\log(a/d)$, define in $z=Z_1/Z_0$
\begin{equation}\label{eq:model}
 \phi_{a,d}=\begin{cases}
 0,& |z|^2\leq R,\\
 a\log|z|^2+C_*-K\log(1+|z|^2),& |z|^2>R,
 \end{cases}\qquad \phi_{a,d}|_D=-\infty.
\end{equation}
The following model and comparisons are unproved target assertions:
$\psi\leq\phi_{a,d}\leq\psi+C_*$.
Write $v\preceq\phi$ for $v\leq\phi+C$ and $v\sim\phi$ for mutual
bounded comparisons, including their common canonical poles.

Let
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 G(x,z)&=\log d_{\rm chord}(x,z)^2+1,
 &w_0&=G*\left(\frac{aH}{m}-a\right),\\
 S_0&=\sup_X(\psi+w_0),
 &d\nu_0&=\frac Hm\,dW.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here $\ddc_xG=\delta_z-\omega_1$ and $\int G(x,z)\omega_1(x)=0$.
Its stated continuity, identities and mean-zero normalization are targets to prove.



A. Independently prove the exact model formula and comparisons, its full product ordinary model property for EVERY specified compact Hermitian Y, its smaller-background envelope and actual finite positive product. No homogeneous action, closedness or BMP on Y is assumed.

B. Independently prove the full divisorial-removal statement, including any additional poles:

Every genuine $v\in\PSH(X,\theta)$ with $v\preceq\psi$ has a unique representation $v=\psi+r$ with
$r\in\PSH(X,\eta)$. Moreover
\[
 \MA_\theta(\psi+r)=\MA_\eta(r),
\]
and ordinary bounded type relative to $\psi$ is equivalent to bounded $r$.


C. Independently prove the entire fixed-reference theorem, including greatestness among ALL allowed singular subsolutions in dimension N and the separated-sector order characterization:

For every $\sigma>0$ there is a greatest genuine finite-mass exponential
solution among all $\theta$-psh exponential subsolutions $v\preceq\phi_{a,d}$:
\[
 \MA_\theta(s_\sigma)=e^{\sigma s_\sigma}f\,dW.
\]
It has ordinary bounded type $s_\sigma\sim\phi_{a,d}$ and is unique in that type.
At poles the exponential is zero; no divisor mass is multiplied by an
infinite weight.

Put $v_\sigma=s_\sigma-\sup_Xs_\sigma$ and
$c_\sigma=e^{\sigma\sup_Xs_\sigma}$. As $\sigma\downarrow0$, the entire family
converges in $L^1(X)$ and locally uniformly on $X\setminus D$:
\[
 v_\sigma\longrightarrow v_0=\psi+w_0-S_0,\qquad
 \MA_\theta(v_0)=c_0 f\,dW,\qquad c_\sigma\longrightarrow c_0.
\]
The limit has ordinary type $\phi_{a,d}$, finite positive mass and belongs
to the exact relative stretching class $\E_{\rm env}(X,\theta,\phi_{a,d})$.
The scalar-centered family converges in the same topologies to
\[
 s_0=\psi+w_0-\int_X(\psi+w_0)\,d\nu_0,
 \qquad s_\sigma-\frac{\log c_0}{\sigma}\longrightarrow s_0,
\]
and the actual scalar error satisfies
\[
 \frac1\sigma\log\frac{c_\sigma}{c_0}
 \longrightarrow S_0-\int_X(\psi+w_0)\,d\nu_0.
\]
Within the separated sector $u=\psi+r(x)\preceq\phi_{a,d}$, $s_0$ is
the greatest critical subsolution satisfying
$\MA_\theta(u)\geq c_0f\,dW$ and $\int_Xu\,d\nu_0\leq0$.
The normalized limit is the unique supremum-zero critical member of this sector.


D. Independently prove the entire varying-reference theorem, including actual limiting ordinary type and every independent parameter rate:

Let $a_j\to a>0$, $d_j\to d>0$, $b_j\to b$ uniformly, with each $b_j$
smooth positive and $b$ smooth positive nonconstant. Let continuous positive
$H_j\to H$ uniformly. For any $\sigma_j>0$ tending to zero, set
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \theta_j&=(a_j+d_j)\omega_1+b_j\kappa,
 &\psi_j&=d_j\log\ell,\\
 \phi_j&=\phi_{a_j,d_j},&f_j&=N b_j^kH_j,\\
 m_j&=\int H_j\omega_1,&c_{0,j}&=a_j/m_j.
 \end{aligned}
\]
The normalized greatest solutions tend in $L^1(X)$ and locally uniformly
off $D$ to $v_0$ from the fixed-reference target C. Their actual measures tend in
total variation to $c_0 f\,dW$. The limit has ordinary bounded type
$\phi_{a,d}$ and the exact relative stretching class.
Writing $c_j=e^{\sigma_j\sup s_j}$, one has
\[
 c_j\to c_0,\qquad
 \frac1{\sigma_j}\log\frac{c_j}{c_{0,j}}
 \longrightarrow S_0-\int(\psi+w_0)d\nu_0,\qquad
 s_j-\frac{\log c_{0,j}}{\sigma_j}\longrightarrow s_0.
\]
There is no restriction on the rates of parameter and exponent variation.


E. Prove nonempty nonclosed examples a=1,d=1/4,b=2+t,H=1, t the standard sphere height: centered limit psi+1/4, normalized limit psi, c0=1 and scalar-error limit1/4. Taking Y=(C2 minus{0})/<z maps to2z> with descended i sum dz_l wedge dbar z_l/|z|^2 rescaled to unit square integral gives an actual compact non-Kahler threefold product and target mass13. Prove its compactness, positivity, non-Kahler obstruction and the exact mass. For a_j=1+sqrt(sigma_j), fixed d,b,H, centering by the limiting scalar1 adds log(1+sqrt(sigma_j))/sigma_j tending to infinity, while centering by c0,j=a_j has a finite error. These are targets, not granted calculations.
